title: Claude de Mondoucet to Charles IX from the Low Countries, 13 July 1572, 4 Jan 1573 and 9 Sept 1573, BnF fr. 16127

plaintext.source: No Court decipherment in fr. 16127; not in Didier's edition (the Reims register begins 6 Sept 1572; Didier's introduction lists this letter as 'chiffrée et en grande partie sans déchiffrement').

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF canvases 125-127, hand transcription at glyph level
transcription.notes: Measured with --drop-first: ct_f60.txt 875 (less 3 bracketed clear words = 872), ct_f60v.txt 44, ct_f61.txt 166; total 1,082 cipher glyphs including nulls. distinct is ct_f60.txt's.

plaintext.source: L. Didier, Lettres et négociations de Claude de Mondoucet, t. 1 (1891), pp. 141-142, from Mondoucet's register (Bibliothèque de Reims); archive.org lettresetngocia01mondgoog. No decipherment in fr. 16127; four interlinear Court glosses on f. 127r only.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF full-resolution canvases 263-265 and strips
transcription.notes: --measure --drop-first gives 1,834 tokens; less 358 word separators '/', '.' and bracketed clear words = 1,476 (NOTES: 1,468). distinct 57 includes '/'. Corrections: 20 glyph edits in the v2 strip re-check plus 4 kept in the v4 constrained pass; 52 signs re-marked as alpha in v3.

plaintext.source: Court decipherment ('deschiffré') ff. 139r-141r, verbatim; verified by glyph-letter alignment.

transcription.notes: Two files: f135r.txt 558 tokens less 117 separators = 441; blk2.txt (ff. 135v-137r) 5,510 less 1,216 separators = 4,294; total 4,735, as in NOTES. Tail f. 137v (c. 21 lines) not transcribed; its decipherment is on f. 141r.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of invented and letter-form signs (one glyph per letter, 24-letter alphabet) with a few digraph and word signs and nulls, inline in clear French.
system.sibling_key: The 1572 key (hand/key2.json) and the 1573 key (f1573/key1573_split2.json) are one system; the 1573 key was seeded from the 1572 one.
system.notes: c. 55 signs in the 1573 key; 23 = qu, crossed phi = ll; word signs (dict, faict, pour, quil, monsieur). Round a and open alpha were first merged; split, alpha = r, round a = l/y/i. Scribe's gaps fall at word boundaries 66% of the time.

prior_solution.where: 9 Sept 1573: Court decipherment on ff. 139-141 (used as known plaintext). 4 Jan 1573: printed in clear by Didier, t. 1 (1891), pp. 141-142, found 21 Sept 2026 after the ciphertext-only passes. 13 July 1572: no reading anywhere known.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with the models and posed the problem with /goal; chose which leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Swept fr. 16127 on Gallica entire: c. 20 Mondoucet cipher despatches 1571-74 with Court decipherments, except 13 July 1572.
Transcribed the verbatim pairs 29 Aug 1572 / f. 9 and 16 July 1572 / f. 64 by hand and by glyph clustering.
Four aligners, each validated on synthetic controls, run on the two pairs.
1.3-1.4 glyphs per letter even on the glossed pair; later traced to a segmenter artefact (hand counts give one glyph per letter).

Hand glyph transcription of 16 July ff. 62r-62v anchored on the interlinear glosses ('pouvez', 'leur délivrance', 'au 30') and the f. 64 decipherment; anchored HMM alignment gave homophone counts, fixed by hand.
Beam decode of the 16 July block with the key reproduced the decipherer's gloss 'leur delivrance des espagnols'.
Decoded 13 July 1572 (ff. 60r, 60v, 61r): reads in stretches (le prince, service du roi, Espaigne, le pape, Angleterre, garnison); transcription-limited.
9 Sept 1573: 4,735 cipher glyphs transcribed and hard-EM-aligned against the Court decipherment ff. 139-141 line for line; ratio 0.91 glyphs/letter, so the decipherment is verbatim, not abridged.
1573 key of c. 55 signs from the 9 Sept alignment, seeded with the 1572 key; same system.
Key re-estimated from 9 Sept block 2 only, block 1 decoded blind: 77% of letters correct (303/391); word-space LM variant 61-64%, dropped.
4 Jan 1573 decoded ciphertext-only with the 1573 key; the gloss 'hambourg' independently reproduced on l. 26; about two-thirds of glyphs in stretches that read.
Re-transcription of all 39 lines of 4 Jan against the strips (v2), 20 glyph edits; small net gain.
Split the a class into round a and open alpha on f135r, f137r and 4 Jan; re-alignment gives alpha = r only; control 77.5% -> 78.3%.

Alpha marked on all five 9 Sept pages (key1573_split2.json, round a = l/y/i); control 79.0%; tryalt constrained pass kept 4 of 11 image-ambiguous alternatives on 4 Jan; best reading 55-60% of letters. Ciphertext-only plateau.

Found the 4 Jan cipher passage printed in clear in Didier, Lettres et négociations de Claude de Mondoucet, t. 1 (1891), pp. 141-142; confirms the decode word for word where it read and fills the gaps. 13 July 1572 not in Didier.
13 July 1572: open alpha marked against round a on the strips of ff. 60r-61r (hand/split.py; 42 of 76 a-class signs are alpha; f. 61 barred o normalised).

Retry: 13 July re-decoded with key2 + alpha = r (1573 counts) and with key1573_split2 directly (hand/decode_retry.py). Control on the 16 July block, not held out: 60.3% -> 61.1% (alpha = r), 56.2% (1573 key), chance 12-15%. 13 July glyphs in stretches reading as sense: ~8% lenient, ~1% strict (hand/decode_retry.txt).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The 1572 key was rebuilt from the glossed 16 July 1572 letter and its decipherment on f. 64, and the 1573 key from aligning the 9 Sept 1573 cipher with the Court's verbatim decipherment on ff. 139-141 of the same volume; that key decoded 4 Jan 1573 to about 55-60% before the letter was found printed in Didier (1891).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Cipher glyphs of the three documents (7,293): 9 Sept (4,735) and 4 Jan (1,476) counted read; 13 July 1572 (1,082) counted at 8 % (87 glyphs), the lenient hand count of stretches reading as sense in hand/decode_retry.txt (strict count 1 %).

gaps.item: 13 July 1572, cipher lines J1-J22 (f. 60r), K1 (f. 60v), M1-M6 (f. 61r)
gaps.detail: No decipherment in fr. 16127 or Didier. After the a/alpha split retry the 1572 key (fitted on one 863-letter crib, ~60% on that block) reads only ~1-8% of the glyphs as sense. The leaves are legible; the limit is the key. f. 61 transcription residue remains but would not read without a better key.

outcome.notes: 9 Sept read by the Court (verified verbatim); 4 Jan read ciphertext-only to ~55-60% of letters, then from print; the project's own contribution is the 1573 key (alpha = r) and the ~79% control.
